title: Quality guardrails gating for Optimize — PRD completion + launch plan (internal beta → limited GA)
creator: Aditya Rao
content:
Context
Optimize can apply cost-saving configuration changes (batching, prefix/KV caching settings, quantization profiles) that can materially affect outputs. We need mandatory quality evaluation checks and regression thresholds before any Optimize recommendation can be applied to production traffic (auto-apply or one-click apply).

This ticket tracks:
- PRD completion and decision points
- Launch sequencing (internal beta → limited GA → GA)
- Cross-functional sign-offs + go/no-go criteria
- External/customer-facing messaging inputs (release notes + exception policy)

- Security/audit/RBAC: Marcus Lin, Kevin Osei

Problem statement
Optimize recommendations are valuable because they reduce unit cost/latency; however they can introduce silent quality regressions. Today, many changes are validated informally or after-the-fact via production monitoring. That is insufficient given:
- Quantization profile switches can change output distribution and introduce rare failures (esp. long-context prompts).
- More aggressive batching/caching can interact with tool/function calling, structured output constraints, and streaming edge cases.
- Customer trust: enterprise procurement requires demonstrable controls (audit logs, approvals, objective thresholds).

Goals (MVP)
1) Safe-by-default: No Optimize apply-to-production without quality gates (except via explicit, time-bound override).
2) Define consistent pass/fail criteria: offline eval deltas vs baseline + minimum coverage/sample sizes.
3) Defense-in-depth enforcement: block at Optimize apply boundary AND block canary promotion when gate fails.
4) Traceability: who/what/why for each proposed change + gate run artifacts + approval/override audit events.
5) Bounded cost/time: tiered gates (fast smoke → full gates) with clear runtime ceilings.

Non-goals (MVP)
- Fully automated private/on-prem enforcement (documented workflow only)
- Overhauling model onboarding / entire eval harness redesign

MVP user stories (must-have)
- As a developer, when I click “Apply recommendation”, the system runs required gates and blocks apply if failed, with clear reasons and artifact links.
- As an ops/platform user, when Optimize is in auto-apply mode for a route, the system runs gates automatically and only applies if passed.
- As an oncall/approver, I can grant a time-bound override with required justification and the action is audit-logged.
- As a rollout owner, I cannot promote a canary if the quality gate has failed for the config diff.

Gating policy decisions (captured for PRD)
- Config change types in scope (MVP):
  - Batching policy updates (continuous batching knobs, max batch tokens / wait windows)
  - Prefix/KV caching settings (enablement + cache behavior toggles)
  - Quantization profile changes (per model family + GPU SKU baseline selection)
- Gate tiers:
  - Smoke gates: fast subset for “low risk” diffs; target <= 20 minutes wall time; small prompt subset with strict failure-on-crash/format violations.
  - Full gates: required for quantization changes and any “risky” runtime knob combos; target <= 2 hours wall time; broader prompt-set coverage and statistical checks.
- Baselines:
  - Default baseline is current production config for the route/model version.
  - Quantization baselines are selected per model family + hardware SKU (avoid comparing apples to oranges).
- Pass/fail:
  - Hard fails: safety/format violations, structured output invalid, tool call contract breakage, crash/OOM, eval harness infra errors beyond retry budget.
  - Soft fails: metric regression beyond threshold with confidence constraints; triggers “failed” unless override.
- Variance handling:
  - Require minimum sample sizes per suite.
  - Use aggregation rules from v1 thresholds doc; track flake score and quarantine workflow for flaky suites.

Launch plan
Phase 0 — Internal alpha (completed)
- Enforcement in staging and internal workloads; focus on correctness + stability.
- Validate: state machine, persistence, artifact plumbing, retry behavior.

Phase 1 — Internal beta (in progress)
Target window: 2026-01 → 2026-02
- Enable gating enforcement for a small set of internal routes (Optimize suggestions for Redwood-hosted API workloads).
- Track: pass rate by config type, average gate runtime, flake rate, retry counts.
- Deliverables:
  - Console surface: gate status summary + deep links to artifacts
  - Runbook + oncall training
  - Initial override policy in place with approver role

Phase 2 — Limited GA (planned)
Target window: late 2026-02 → early 2026-03
- Expand to a subset of external accounts (self-serve + 1–3 design partners) on hosted API.
- Default behavior: gates required; overrides allowed only for enterprise tiers and only with time-bound expiration.
- Rollout: progressive enablement by account tier + route.

Phase 3 — GA + expansion (planned)
Target window: 2026-03+
- Expand coverage to more model families/hardware SKUs.
- Expand to Dedicated defaults.
- Private deployment workflow: documented + manual enforcement with audit logging; automation later.

Go / No-go criteria for Limited GA
Functional
- Apply is blocked when gate fails (Optimize API) and canary promotion blocked on failure (rollout controller).
- Gate results are visible in Console with artifact links; errors are actionable.
- Overrides are time-bound, require justification, and write audit events.
- Static pre-gate validation blocks unsupported/risky diffs before spending GPU time.

Quality / stats
- For supported prompt sets: stable thresholds with < 5% false-positive “regression” rate on known-safe diffs (tracked via internal beta replay).
- Flake rate: <= 2% of gate runs require manual triage; quarantine path works.

Performance / cost
- Smoke gates p50 <= 20 min; p95 <= 35 min.
- Full gates p50 <= 90 min; p95 <= 120 min.
- Eval GPU spend is within budget envelope (tracked weekly) and does not starve other critical jobs.

Reliability / ops
- Gate execution SLO and alerting in place (no paging storms due to flaky suites).
- Runbook validated with at least one rehearsal scenario.
- Regional capacity: no sustained timeouts in eu-west (watch for repeat of prior incidents).

Security / compliance
- RBAC: override approver role gated and auditable.
- Audit log events exportable for enterprise customers (SIEM-friendly fields).

Cross-functional sign-offs (required)
- Applied ML/Evals: Jonas Weber / Karthik Iyer / Selene Huang / Sana Farid
- Runtime safety: Mateo Alvarez / Noah Patel
- SRE/Observability: Sean Gallagher / Allison Grant
- Rollouts: Paula Mendes / Jada Williams
- Security: Marcus Lin
- Console UX: Dylan Brooks / Kenji Nakamura

Risks / open questions
1) Flaky prompt sets causing blocked improvements
- Mitigation: flake scoring + quarantine workflow; explicit infra-error vs quality-regression classification; rerun policy.

2) Quantization regressions only visible under long-context or rare prompts
- Mitigation: add long-context “hard case” suite; require full gates for quant diffs; raise coverage minimums for long-context routes.

3) Gate runtime too slow and blocks day-to-day iteration
- Mitigation: smoke gates first; allow “evaluate only” mode; parallelization knobs; cap eval cost and queue latency; region-aware scheduling.

4) Policy complexity (per-route / per-tier / per-model)
- Mitigation: ship conservative default policy and allow opt-down only with explicit approval; keep policy versioned.

5) Overrides abused
- Mitigation: strict approver list, short expiration, required follow-up ticket, dashboard of overrides, weekly review.

Customer communication plan (draft)
- Internal beta notes (eng + CS): emphasize stricter controls; how to interpret failures; where artifacts live; how to request override.
- Limited GA messaging to design partners:
  - “Optimize cost savings now come with mandatory quality checks.”
  - “If a gate fails, the system blocks apply and shows why.”
  - “Overrides exist but are time-bound and audited.”
- External docs: add section in Optimize docs for quality gates + interpreting results + override process.

Acceptance criteria for closing this PM ticket
- PRD finalized in Confluence with:
  - clear MVP scope + non-goals
  - go/no-go criteria
  - launch sequencing and enablement plan
  - explicit override policy link
  - ownership + escalation paths
- Limited GA launch checklist created and agreed by PM/Eng/SRE/Security.
- Cross-functional sign-offs recorded in updates section below.
